notes:
Summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS. Started with Redwood hosted API trial (Q4/2025) to validate integration and latency. Positive functional results; now moving to Dedicated sizing + pricing.

Hosted trial notes:
- Trial window: 2025-12-01 -> 2026-02-28. Integrated via SDK (server-side) and one client-side embed for demo.
- Workloads run: primary = real-time support chat assistant; secondary = document search (embeddings) for knowledge base; occasional reranking for recommendations.
- Integration comment from PM: "responses were better than previous endpoint, latency OK for MVP but need firm p99 SLOs".
- Security: asked for SSO/SAML + audit logs, KMS for key management, paper trail for data residency in US and EU. Legal did initial questionnaire 2026-02-20.

Traffic & token observations (hosted trial):
- Monthly active end-users (prod-like pilot): ~11k.
- Average daily active: ~1.2k.
- Peak observed QPS during business hours: ~18 QPS (sustained spikes up to 22 for ~30m during campaign).
- Typical steady-state QPS: 6-9 QPS across region (US-east primary).
- Observed concurrency: average concurrency ~3-5, peak concurrency ~12-14.
- Token mix (by volume): chat generation ~70% of total tokens, embeddings ~25%, reranking/other ~5%.
- Avg tokens per chat request: ~800 (prompt ~550, completion ~250). Embedding invocations small payloads (~120 tokens avg).
- Monthly token volume: trial aggregated ~85M tokens (est).

POC / sizing asks:
- Customer wants Redwood proposal for Dedicated capacity to meet: p95 latency goal for chat < 350ms, p99 < 900ms under target load; sustained QPS target = 20, burst to 40 for promotional events.
- Wants redundancy across 2 AZs; option to scale up for month-long campaigns.
- Preference: predictable reserved pool + autoscale burst buffer.
- Request: 2 sizing options — conservative (handles 20 sustained QPS + 40 burst) and aggressive (handles 50 sustained QPS). Include cost delta and expected unit token cost.

Commercial / pricing signals:
- Procurement cycle: budget planning in April; likely commit to 12-month reserved if numbers meet unit economics.
- Price sensitivity: high. Asked for per-token blended pricing and breakouts for embeddings vs chat.
- Will consider Redwood Optimize add-on for batching/quantization recommendations to reduce unit costs.

Recent activity timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-15: Kickoff / integration call (AE + SE) — baseline metrics captured.
- 2026-01-28: Hosted trial SDK rollout complete (internal staging -> limited prod).
- 2026-02-20: Security questionnaire submitted; legal questions around EU residency.
- 2026-02-25: Fireflies demo + POC debrief (ff_20260203_tb-demo-01).
- 2026-03-02: Team asked for dedicated sizing + cost estimate (email thread gt-20260302-pricing-ask).
- 2026-03-08: Internal Redwood pre-pricing alignment meeting (AE/SE/Finance).

Customer quotes / flavor:
- PM: "We like the predictability but need lower p99 for chat to roll to all customers."
- Infra lead: "Show us concrete GPU-node equivalent and expected QPS per node; we need to justify the spend to finance."

Next steps / owner actions:
- SE (Liam) to run model/latency profile with customer's token distribution and propose node sizing (due 2026-03-16).
- AE (Ava) to schedule infra sizing call 2026-03-18 with customer's infra + finance.
- Deliver formal Dedicated proposal (conservative + aggressive) + 12-month pricing options and Optimize addon scenarios.

Notes shorthand / quick follow-ups:
- Customer will share per-route token logs (anonymized) by 2026-03-12.
- Ask product: confirm supported fallback model variants and cost delta.
- Legal: tracking data residency checklist; EU residency required for subset of EU customers.
traffic_forecast: Baseline: sustain 20 QPS (business hours), burst 40 QPS for campaigns; concurrency typical 3-5, peak 12-14. Monthly token forecast (12mo pro-forma): 85M -> 1.0B tokens depending on growth scenarios. Token mix: chat 70%, embeddings 25%, rerank 5%.
demo_results: Functionality: pass. Latency: p95 ~310ms during trial; p99 spiked to ~1.2s under campaign load. Stability: no hard errors, occasional timeouts during 22 QPS spikes. SE notes: batching could reduce cost by ~18% for chat workload; caching recommended for ~30% of queries.
